questions.stem: A surveyor walks 107 km north, turns right and walks 228 km, then turns right and walks 12 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 247. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 95 km along the initial direction and 228 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(95² + 228²) = 247 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 26 km east, turns right and walks 45 km, then turns right and walks 2 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 51. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 24 km along the initial direction and 45 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(24² + 45²) = 51 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 48 km west, turns right and walks 96 km, then turns right and walks 8 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 104. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 40 km along the initial direction and 96 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(40² + 96²) = 104 km.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
banking savings digital = vo mi ze
banking secure rural = vo ni pa
savings secure growth = to mi pa
digital rural growth = ze to ni
banking savings growth = to vo mi
What is the code for “banking”?
questions.explanation: Answer: vo. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: banking = vo, savings = mi, digital = ze, secure = pa, rural = ni, growth = to.

questions.stem: E is the mother of A. B is the daughter of A. F is the father of A. How is B related to F?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. F is a parent of A, and B is A’s daughter. Hence B is F’s grandchild.

questions.stem: D is the brother of G. G is the mother of H. F is the father of D and G. How is D related to H?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. D is the brother of H’s mother G. Therefore D is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: D is the only daughter of F. F is the father of D. B is the son of D. A is the sister of F. How is F related to B?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. F is the father of D, and D is B’s mother. Thus F is the maternal grandfather.

questions.explanation: Answer: 162000. Profit ratio is 36:24. Each ratio unit = ₹2700. Total = 60 × 2700.

questions.stem: A boat covers 220 km in still water in 10 hours. If the stream flows at 4 km/h, how far (km) can it travel upstream in 5 hours?
questions.explanation: Answer: 90. Still-water speed = 22 km/h. Upstream speed = 22 − 4. Distance = speed × 5.

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes can fill a tank in 68 and 102 hours. An outlet empties it in 170 hours. All three open together. Find the time (hours) to fill the empty tank. (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 53.68. Net rate = 1/68 + 1/102 − 1/170 = 19/1020 tank/hour. Required time = 53.68 hours.

questions.stem: A is twice as old as B. After 9 years their ages will be in ratio 3:2. What is the present sum of their ages?
questions.explanation: Answer: 27. Let B = x, A = 2x. (2x+9)/(x+9) = 3/2 gives x = 9. Present sum = 3x.

questions.stem: Two articles are sold for ₹3200 each. One earns 10% profit and the other incurs 10% loss. Find the combined cost price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 6464.65. Recover each cost separately: 3200×100/110 + 3200×100/90. Equal selling prices do not imply equal costs.

questions.stem: [Caselet set] The combined total at A and D is what percentage more or less than the total at C? Give the absolute percentage difference, rounded to two decimals.

questions.stem: A sum of ₹17000 earns ₹5100 simple interest in 3 years. At the same annual rate, what would be the amount (₹) after 2 years with annual compounding?
questions.explanation: Answer: 20570. Rate = interest ×100/(principal ×3) = 10%. Compound amount = 17000 × (1 + 10/100)².
